anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level statements and transaction scopes are written in a way that forces the engine to process, lock, or return more data than the business logic actually requires.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : The optimizer’s metadata is stale or incomplete, leading to systematic cardinality misestimation and poor plan choices.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : Physical pages or index structures are corrupted or internally inconsistent, making on-disk data no longer fully trustworthy.

When these three root causes coexist, the database can exhibit an unusually wide spectrum of symptoms: extreme and highly variable statement latency, repeated slow-query log entries, sudden switches from index seeks to full table scans, estimator-vs-actual row count gaps that grow with each plan execution, unexpected duplicate or missing rows in result sets, CRC or page-checksum errors surfacing only on certain access paths, frequent plan recompilations, and cascading application timeouts or deadlocks as long-running transactions collide with corruption-triggered lock escalations or error retries. Because each anomaly can mask or amplify the others, the operational picture becomes noisy—making it difficult to tell whether performance, correctness, or physical health is the primary issue on any given statement.

Causal interaction: poorly written workload patterns generate oversized scans, floods of singleton lookups, and long-lived transactions that churn large portions of the data set. This high change rate prevents automatic statistics thresholds from firing in time and accelerates divergence between real and recorded data distributions, which in turn pushes the optimizer toward plans that touch even more pages. The broadened I/O surface area increases the likelihood of hitting latent corrupt pages or split-brain index chains. Once corruption is encountered, the engine may invalidate or bypass indexes, forcing further full scans that magnify both the workload stress and the statistical drift. The feedback loop—inefficient workload causing stale statistics, stale statistics producing expansionary plans, and those plans exposing corruption that then eliminates efficient access paths—rapidly degrades overall performance and reliability, while making root-cause isolation far more complex.

entry.official_description: CREATE TABLE... SELECT...  on a table with an auto-increment column is unsafe because the order in which rows are retrieved by the SELECT determines which (if any) rows are inserted. This order cannot be predicted and may differ on source and the replica.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with log shipping, replica apply state, replication-channel configuration, or cross-node communication needed to keep replicated state consistent.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver state, log retention, downstream apply lag, and network stability between replication endpoints.
